data.description:
## Context

The root tree holds 6,008 flat ticket directories and is 270 KB; every commit re-emits the WHOLE
root tree, so tree bytes are ~95% of the blobless pack. Sharding the flat namespace shrinks the
per-commit root-tree object so each re-emission is far smaller — a durable structural reduction of
the tree churn that dominates the pack, complementing S1 (historical) and W1 (write-rate).

## Scope

Shard the flat `tickets/<id>` layout into a fan-out namespace (e.g. `tickets/<quad-prefix>/<id>`)
so a mutation re-emits only a small shard subtree plus a small top-level tree, not a 270 KB flat
root. Preserve ticket resolution (alias/short-id/full-id), event replay, and reconcile behavior.
Requires a migration path for existing ticket paths.

## Out of scope

The history reclaim (S1) and the write-batching (W1). This is the on-disk tree LAYOUT.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Ticket storage uses a sharded fan-out layout; a single mutation re-emits only its shard subtree + a small top-level tree (measured tree bytes per commit drop substantially vs the 270 KB flat root).
- [ ] Ticket resolution (alias, short-id, full-id) and event replay are unchanged (existing resolver/replay tests pass).
- [ ] A migration maps existing flat paths to the sharded layout without losing or reassigning any ticket identity.
- [ ] Reconcile/merge-as-union behavior is preserved on a reconvergence fixture.

## Portability

Pure store-layout change with an in-process migration; no dependence on any single CI provider.
data.title: W2: shard the 6,008 flat ticket dirs to cut per-commit root-tree churn
